title: OneDrive and SharePoint: anchored comments in the PDF viewer on the web
summary: Hold: the prose understates the documented scope of the tenant commenting control by saying its coverage of PDF comments is not stated. Microsoft describes the control as disabling or enabling commenting on files; the roadmap facts and PowerShell call are correct. The licensing field also needs to distinguish published product licensing from unpublished feature-specific terms.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the planned anchored PDF comments, and the cited PDF features page does not mention them.
claims.quote: Searched: "OneDrive" "anchored comments" PDF; OneDrive SharePoint anchored PDF viewer comments storage downloaded shared comments licence. Read onedrive-pdf-features in full; results describe markup, Syntex annotations or SharePoint Embedded, not this anchored-comment feature.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence statement specific to anchored PDF comments is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive SharePoint PDF anchored comments licence licensing price meter. Read onedrive-pdf-features and OneDrive/SharePoint service descriptions; search excerpts covered document-processing meters and Syntex annotations, not anchored PDF comments.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because feature-specific terms have not been published.
claims.quote: OneDrive is included in Microsoft 365 and Office 365 plans, in SharePoint plans, and can also be purchased as a standalone plan.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included". Add to licensing.notes: "OneDrive is included in Microsoft 365 and Office 365 plans and SharePoint plans, or can be purchased standalone. Organisation users accessing SharePoint need a licence that includes SharePoint; no licence terms specific to anchored PDF comments are published." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/onedrive-for-business-service-description and https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/sharepoint-online-service-description/sharepoint-online-service-description, which states: "To access SharePoint, users in your organization need to be assigned a license that includes SharePoint." Retain the existing distinction between free annotation tools and anchored comments.

claims.claim: The correctly documented file-commenting control is qualified as not confirmed to apply to new PDF viewer comments.
claims.quote: Disables or enables commenting functionality on the files. PARAMVALUE: True | False
claims.fix: Set controls[0].governs to "Whether commenting on files is disabled for the tenant". Set its note to "Disables or enables commenting functionality on files. The reference states its general reach without excluding PDFs; keep pilot testing as wiki advice rather than a claim that applicability is undocumented.

claims.where: Governance controls: paragraph beginning Only one control
claims.claim: Whether the tenant-wide file-commenting parameter governs new PDF viewer comments is not stated.
claims.quote: Disables or enables commenting functionality on the files. PARAMVALUE: True | False
claims.fix: Replace "Whether it governs the new PDF viewer comments is not stated and should be confirmed by testing." with "The reference describes its reach as commenting functionality on files; test the PDF viewer experience in a pilot before relying on the control." This preserves the testing advice without reporting the documented file-commenting scope as absent.
